description: CosmoCare is a solo project focused on health monitoring for astronauts during long-duration space missions. I am a STEM undergrad interested in human health and space biology.
summary:
CosmoCare is a browser-based health-monitoring prototype designed to explore astronaut wellbeing during long-duration space missions. Astronauts may experience physiological and psychological challenges, including cardiovascular changes, disrupted sleep and stress.

The prototype allows users to enter four health indicators: heart rate, blood oxygen saturation (SpO₂), sleep duration and self-reported stress. It compares these readings against illustrative baseline values and displays a simple health summary highlighting selected deviations.

CosmoCare aims to demonstrate how accessible digital tools could support health awareness during space missions. The current version uses simulated, manually entered readings and is an educational proof of concept, not a clinically validated medical system.
details:
CosmoCare is a browser-based prototype that explores how digital health-monitoring tools could support astronaut wellbeing during long-duration space missions. Problem Addressed - Spaceflight can involve physiological and psychological challenges, including cardiovascular adaptations, sleep disruption, isolation and stress. Monitoring changes in health indicators is an important part of understanding astronaut wellbeing. How CosmoCare Works - The prototype provides a dashboard with four manually entered health indicators: - Heart rate (BPM) - Blood oxygen saturation (SpO₂) - Sleep duration (hours) - Self-reported stress level (1–10) Users enter their readings and select "Analyse My Readings". JavaScript compares the inputs against illustrative baseline values and generates a health summary highlighting selected deviations. Technology and Development - The prototype was developed using HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with CodePen used for development and testing. HTML structures the interface, CSS provides the visual design, and JavaScript handles user inputs and rule-based comparisons. NASA Research Relevance - NASA Human Research Program resources informed the project's focus on cardiovascular health, sleep and behavioural wellbeing during spaceflight. NASA's Open Science Data Repository was also identified as a relevant resource for potential future development. No NASA dataset or live astronaut sensor data is currently integrated into the prototype. Benefits and Future Scope - CosmoCare demonstrates a simple and accessible approach to presenting health readings. Future improvements could include wearable sensor integration, personalised baselines, historical trend visualisation and analysis of relevant spaceflight datasets.

The current version is an educational proof of concept using simulated, manually entered readings. It is not a medical diagnostic or clinically validated monitoring system.
